text: In the third month after leaving Egypt, on that very day, Israel reached the wilderness of Sinai.
They had traveled on from Rephidim, entered the Sinai wilderness, and made camp there, facing the mountain.
Moses went up the mountain to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: Tell this to the family of Jacob, the people of Israel:
You saw what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Now if you truly obey me and keep my covenant, you will be my own treasured possession out of all the nations — the whole earth is mine,
and you will become a kingdom of priests for me, a holy nation. Tell this to the Israelites.
Moses came down, called together the elders of the people, and laid out everything the LORD had commanded him.
All the people answered together, We will do everything the LORD has said. So Moses brought their answer back to the LORD.
The LORD told Moses, I am going to come to you in a thick cloud, so the people will hear me speaking with you and will always trust you. And Moses reported the people's words to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, Go to the people and set them apart today and tomorrow; have them wash their clothes,
and be ready by the third day, because on that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in full view of all the people.
Mark off a boundary around the mountain for the people and tell them: Be careful not to go up the mountain or even touch its edge — anyone who touches the mountain must be put to death.
No hand may touch that person; he must be stoned or shot with arrows, whether man or animal — he will not be allowed to live. Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they go up the mountain.
Moses went down from the mountain to the people, set them apart, and they washed their clothes.
He told the people, Be ready by the third day; do not come near your wives.
On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast, and everyone in the camp trembled.
Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was covered in smoke, because the LORD had come down on it in fire; the smoke rose like smoke from a furnace, and the whole mountain shook violently.
The trumpet blast grew louder and louder; Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
The LORD came down on the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses up to the summit, and Moses went up.
The LORD told Moses, Go down and warn the people not to break through to stare at the LORD, or many of them will die.
Even the priests who come near the LORD must set themselves apart, or the LORD will break out against them.
Moses said to the LORD, The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, because you already warned us to mark off the mountain and set it apart.
The LORD told him, Go down, then come back up bringing Aaron with you — but the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them.
So Moses went down to the people and told them.
